Name: Louis-Kennedy Osinachi Ilobinso
Message:
Felicitation on 15 Years of Priestly Ministry

Dear Rev. Fr. Maximillian Nwosu,

Nwannem,

With immense joy, gratitude to God, and a heart filled with fond memories, I congratulate you on the remarkable milestone of 15 years of faithful service in the Catholic priesthood.

Our story goes back more than three decades. I have known you since I was about ten years old. We received the Sacrament of the Holy Eucharist on the same day, and around the same period, we became altar boys at Christ the King Cathedral, Aba. Little did we know then that the friendship and shared journey that began in our childhood would take us through such an extraordinary path.

You entered the Minor Seminary in 1992, a year before I joined you in 1993. We eventually found ourselves entering the Major Seminary almost at the same time in 2000. Then came the difficult period in 2003, when our congregation was experiencing a crisis and we were all sent to our Mother House in Ohuru for a compulsory one-year novitiate programme.

It was during that challenging chapter that about seven of us made the difficult decision to abandon our journey toward the priesthood. We left the novitiate and proceeded to the secular university to complete our philosophical studies. Of all of us who took that path, only one eventually returned to the congregation and persevered to the end.

That person is no other than you, Very Rev. Fr. Maximillian Nwosu.

Your return was not merely a return to a religious congregation; it was a return to a calling. Your story is therefore a powerful testimony of perseverance, discernment, grace, and God's mysterious ways. What we once journeyed through together as young men eventually became, for you, a vocation to serve God's people at the altar.

Fr. Max, nwannem, I am deeply proud to be associated with you and to call you my childhood friend and contemporary. You are, indeed, a full dose of a refined gentleman—gracious, humble, warm-hearted, and deeply committed to your vocation.

In you, I see the qualities of a religious sanguine and the fecundity of a great missionary. I see a man whose journey reminds us that when God calls, He also gives the grace to persevere, even when the road becomes uncertain or difficult.

Fifteen years ago, you made your priestly vows and entrusted yourself completely to God's promise and providence. Today, as you celebrate this beautiful anniversary, may the same God who called you, sustained you, and brought you this far continue to renew your strength and deepen your joy in ministry.

May your priesthood continue to bear abundant fruit. May God bless you with wisdom, good health, peace, courage, and renewed apostolic zeal. May He make your ministry a source of healing, hope, and transformation to countless souls. May your life and priesthood continue to inspire young people who are discerning their own vocation.

And whenever you look back at the journey—from two little boys serving at the altar at Christ the King Cathedral, Aba, to the priesthood you have faithfully embraced for fifteen years—may you always see the unmistakable fingerprints of God.

Congratulations, Fr. Max, on 15 years of working in God's vineyard.

May the years ahead be even more fruitful than those behind you. May you continue to prosper in His blessings, remain steadfast in His service, and finish the race with joy and fulfilment.

Ad multos annos, my dear friend and brother!

With heartfelt congratulations, admiration, and fraternal affection,

Louis-Kennedy Osinachi Ilobinso
